newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-German and French shares boosted by Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German and French shares boosted by Dow.

text.p: German stocks closed at new record highs on Monday and the Paris bourse ended firmer as Wall Street moved ahead again following its storming close last week.

In currency dealing the dollar recovered from troughs against the mark and yen in late Europe after ambling sideways in narrow dealings, but the market was subdued because of a market holiday in Britain.
The Dow was up around 25 points when European trading drew to a close. This follows its 94.72 point or 1.36 percent rise to a new peak on Friday.
This was enough to help push Frankfurt's Dax index of floor trading and the IBIS Dax index of electronic trade to new records.

The 30-share DAX comfortably exceeded a previous record high of 3,474.28 points to end bourse up 68.41 points, or nearly two percent at 3,528.78 points, just off an all-time high of 3,533.18 points reached earlier in the session. The IBIS Dax ended at 3,565 points, up around 2.1 percent.

Dealers said trade was also underpinned by the continuing strength of the dollar -- good for German exports -- and Dax futures. Automobile stocks had led the way but trading volumes were limited by the absence of London-based investors.
"After the massive jump in the first quarter, people seemed to be a bit nervous and April seemed to be a bit of a consolidation phase," one trader said.
"If we don't get any massive dirt from the U.S. this may be sustainable," he added.

One shadow in Germany was caused by shares in computer software maker SAP, which plummeted as much as five percent in early trade after prosecutors said they were investigating a potentially serious case of insider trading in the stock. However they regained ground and closed up 3.10 marks at 324.50, a rise which still lagged behind the broader market.
French shares closed higher supported by Wall Street, but trading in Paris also suffered from low volumes because of the absence of London, Europe's biggest stock exchange.

The market earlier took heart from an opinion poll putting the centre-right coalition in a comfortable-but-reduced lead over the Socialists. Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he thought the election contest was getting closer.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.53 points or 0.66 percent at 2,672.84.
Currency trading was particularly quiet in the absence of London.
"There is not much going on. The markets are very quiet and we are stuck in a small ranges," said a trader at a German bank.
One focus of interest was sterling following the British general election.
At 1600 GMT sterling was trading at 2.8065 marks against session lows of 2.7975 and late Friday's 2.8052 marks.
Traders were watching as the new Labour government under Prime Minister Tony Blair as it began its first full week of power.

They were focusing on Wednesday's British monetary meeting between new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and Bank of England Governor Eddie George amid speculation Brown will sanction the interest rate rise the BoE has long been urging.
STOCKS, CLOSING INDICES
The Paris CAC-40 index closed up 17.53 points at 2,672.84.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 68.41 points at 3,528.78.
The London market was closed for a public holiday. On Friday the FTSE 100 closed up 10.6 points at 4,455.6.
CURRENCIES AT 1615 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7320 marks compared with 1.7273 marks late in Europe on Friday. It was at 126.65 yen after 126.63 yen late on Friday.
PRECIOUS METALS
The London gold market was closed for a holiday on Monday. It closed at around $340.05 an ounce on Friday. In New York on Monday the COMEX gold prices was around $343.80 at 1400 gmt.
